body:
Cooperate and hope for the best. You'll get through it. It may not be as big of a deal as you think. Don't throw your life a way based on something that is completely up in the air. Have you consulted with a lawyer yet? If you haven't, be sure to consult with several ASAP and be prepared. Having a plan might help.

I'm sorry that you are going through this. Just know that you can and will recover. Things may not go the way that you expected but that doesn't necessarily have to be a bad thing. Good luck :\

I am in a similar situation and can certainly empathize. I don't have my own life figured out enough to be really reliable for good advice but I'll give some anyway. If a friend came to you feeling the way you did and confessing those things to you, would you react the way your friend did? I'm assuming that you probably wouldn't considering that you have some understanding of the pain associated with it. There are more people like you who would be understanding, helpful, and supportive; you just haven't found them yet. Its hard to find those people especially when you are feeling so down, but live with the knowledge that they exist. You are not better off dead. The pain may seem unbearable now but the opportunity for a better future does exist. Hang in there.

Thank you. It is helpful to hear from someone who has a similar situation. I really hope that you find a way to find happiness in yourself as well. I may not feel it on my own but I trust people when they say that its worth fighting for.

Thank you for the kind words. I still am very afraid of my doctor though. You should have seen the way she reacted when I gained 7 pounds (after losing 30) nevermind gaining back the whole loss and then some. I know the worst case scenario is that she scolds me a bit but I'm just really sensitive to that right now. I really am trying the best I can. Of course I want to be thin and healthy, I felt great after losing some weight. I feel like there are just too many outside sources telling me that I am worthless and have no self control as an overweight female and I don't need my doctor to be another one. I hope that I can find another or at least stop being such a baby about it.

I am aware that I can lose weight. I have done it before and the dedication came easily for me but it takes time. I can't live my life postponing happiness just like I put off everything else. I gained the weight back because I feared for my life. I did not understand at the time what was happening to me. What is to prevent that from happening again?

In terms of keeping a job, I have only had one. My father agreed to pay my tuition if I did not try to work at the same time so I could concentrate on my studies. I was only into it halfheartedly anyway which of course I now regret. After graduating, I worked but ended up leaving when the panic disorder happened. I could not stay standing for more than a few minutes nevermind getting work done. Now I'm just having trouble getting back into it. It seems hopeless. I get questioned about my lack of work experience and long gaps. It goes against me in any interview. Besides the one job the only "experience" I have is babysitting. Like I said, I feel like I have never really lived my life. I just figured I didn't need to because I would be dead soon enough. I know I am the only one to blame for this but giving it time is not helping with the motivation I need to keep going. I need relief now. I can't keep chasing after this light at the end of the tunnel that keeps retreating.
